displays.title: Your screens
displays.intro: One row per physical screen. The Main screen is the forward window: its size and distance decide the field of view the sim gets. Side and overhead screens are listed for the Multi Window read-out only.
displays.none: No screens yet. Add the forward one first.
displays.oneMain: Exactly one screen must have the role Main — {0} found. Nothing can be applied until that is fixed.

role.label: Role
role.hint: Main = the forward window. Left, Right and Overhead are Multi Window screens.

name.label: Name
name.hint: A label for this list, for example Main or Left TV.

diagonal.label: Diagonal (in)
diagonal.hint: The screen size on the box, in inches. Tick the box below to enter centimetres instead.

aspectWidth.label: Aspect width
aspectWidth.hint: The shape of the screen: 16 and 9 for a 16:9 TV, 21 and 9 for an ultrawide, 4 and 3 for an old monitor.

aspectHeight.label: Aspect height
aspectHeight.hint: The second number of the aspect ratio (9 of 16:9).

distance.label: Distance (m)
distance.hint: From your eye to the centre of the screen, in metres, measured straight at it.

yaw.label: Yaw (°)
yaw.hint: Where the screen's centre is, left or right of straight ahead. 0 for the forward screen; positive = to the right.

centreAboveEye.label: Centre above eye (m)
centreAboveEye.hint: How far the screen's centre sits above your eye, in metres. Negative when it is below. 0 when it is level.

apply.title: How real
apply.confirm: Write InitialZoom {0} into this file? A backup is made first.

realism.label: Realism
realism.hint: 100 % = the view is life-size on your Main screen. 0 % = the sim's default view. Anything between is a blend.
realism.more: A hardware cockpit with the TV as the forward window wants 100 %, even though that is much tighter than the default — you see exactly what you would see through the real window. A desk setup may prefer less so more of the world stays in view.

applyPitch.label: Also tilt the camera
applyPitch.hint: Writes the camera pitch so a screen whose centre is above or below your eye is looked at straight. Off keeps the pitch of your saved view.

readout.title: What will be written
readout.invalid: A screen has a size, aspect or distance of zero. Fix it on the Displays section.

file.title: The saved pilot view
file.hint: Only this file is ever changed
file.label: File
file.pickHint: The custom camera file MSFS 2024 saved for this aircraft. Newest first. Files under Official and Community are never touched.
file.hintTitle: Aircraft reported by ProSim: {0}. Folders whose name matches it are listed first; if none matches, every aircraft is shown.
file.hintNone: ProSim has not reported an aircraft yet, so every aircraft folder is listed.
file.noRoot: No MSFS 2024 LocalCache folder was found on this PC. Run the app on the PC that runs the simulator.
file.noneTitle: No saved pilot view yet. Make one first:
file.step2: Put the cockpit view where you want it.
file.step3: Press Ctrl+F10 (VFR Pilot View Save). MSFS creates the camera file.
file.step4: Come back here and press Refresh.

result.nudgeOk: Applied live — the cockpit view was reset.
result.nudgeFailed: Not applied live. It takes effect on the next aircraft load.
result.noBlocks: The file holds no cockpit pilot view, so nothing was written. Save the view in the sim (Ctrl+F10) and refresh.
result.verify1: Options → General → Developers → Developer Mode on.
result.verify2: Dev menu: Debug → Aircraft → Camera Blend.

multi.title: Multi Window
multi.note: MSFS 2024 renders every window with one field of view: the Main screen's. Type these rotations into the Multi Window dialog; the FOV you see there is what the Apply section wrote. The delta shows how far a side screen of a different size is from its own ideal.
multi.shared: Shared vertical FOV for every window: {0}°
multi.none: No side or overhead screens configured.

cp.title: ChasePlane
cp.notDetected: ChasePlane for MSFS 2024 was not detected on this PC.
cp.detected: ChasePlane for MSFS 2024 is installed. Its cockpit presets carry their own zoom and override the native view when you recall them — the file this page writes is not what ChasePlane shows.
cp.target: To match it in ChasePlane, adjust the cockpit preset's zoom until the dev-mode Fov reads {0} rad ({1}° vertical).
cp.advice: Simplest: leave the cockpit view native (do not recall a ChasePlane cockpit preset) and use ChasePlane for the external cameras. Nothing here ever writes to ChasePlane's files.
